text: The Titanic may have been let down by its rivets.
About three million of them held its plates together.
Along the middle, machines pressed in strong steel rivets. But at the curved bow, the machines couldn't fit, so workers hammered in wrought iron by hand.
Rivets from the wreck were full of slag, glassy leftovers that can make iron brittle.
When the iceberg shoved the bow, heads could snap off, and the seams opened.
And that was only one link in the chain. Full video on my channel.
